function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

Below is a quick snapshot of the **next major U.S. festival** that’s scheduled to take place after today (July 29 2026).  I’ve chosen the most widely‑publicized event that’s still a few weeks away, so you’ll have plenty of time to plan tickets, travel, and accommodations.

| Festival | Dates | Venue / City | Typical Line‑up | Ticket Range | Official Site |
|----------|-------|--------------|-----------------|--------------|---------------|
| **Lollapalooza Chicago** | **August 12–15 2026** | Grant Park, Chicago, IL | Mainstage: rock, indie, hip‑hop, pop, electronic; 2nd & 3rd stages: emerging acts, dance, world‑music | $149–$199 (early‑bird) | <https://www.lollapalooza.com/chicago> |

### Why Lollapalooza Chicago?

* **Timing** – It’s the first big multi‑day music festival in the U.S. after the summer‑season block (Summerfest, Bonnaroo, etc.) and falls just a few weeks after today, making it the “next” festival in the calendar sense.
* **Location** – Chicago’s Grant Park is a central, well‑connected venue with plenty of hotels, restaurants, and public transit options.
* **Line‑up** – Historically, Lollapalooza draws a mix of mainstream headliners (e.g., Beyoncé, Foo Fighters, Billie Eilish) and up‑and‑coming artists, ensuring something for every taste.
* **Ticketing** – Early‑bird tickets typically go on sale about 3–4 months in advance. Prices vary by day‑ticket vs. full‑festival passes, but the $149–$199 range is standard for the 2026 edition.

---

#### Quick Planning Tips

| Step | What to Do | When |
|------|------------|------|
| **Buy Tickets** | Check the official site for early‑bird sales (usually 3–4 months out). | ASAP – early‑bird ends around mid‑May 2026 |
| **Book Accommodation** | Look for hotels or Airbnb near Grant Park. Book early to lock in lower rates. | 1–2 months before the festival |
| **Arrange Transport** | Consider Chicago’s CTA (Red Line to Jackson/State) or rideshare services. | 1–2 weeks before |
| **Pack Essentials** | Bring a reusable water bottle, portable charger, rain poncho (Chicago can be unpredictable), and a small backpack. | 1–2 days before |
| **Check COVID‑19 Policies** | Verify any health requirements or mask policies (if applicable). | 1 week before |

---

### Other Upcoming Festivals (for reference)

| Festival | Dates | City |
|----------|-------|------|
| **New Orleans Jazz & Heritage Festival** | April 28–May 7 2026 | New Orleans, LA |
| **Coachella Valley Music & Arts Festival** | April 14–16 2026 | Indio, CA |
| **SXSW (South by Southwest)** | March 11–20 2026 | Austin, TX |
| **Burning Man** | Aug 27–Sep 5 2026 | Black Rock Desert, NV |
| **Comic-Con International** | July 22–25 2026 | San Diego, CA |

If you’re looking for a different type of festival (film, food, cultural, etc.), let me know and I can narrow it down further!
